cards.title: This Sea Slug Can Sever Its Own Head and Regrow a Brand-New Body
cards.body: In a bizarre feat of survival, the sacoglossan sea slug Elysia marginata can cleanly sever its own head from its body. While the headless body eventually dies, the severed head crawls away, surviving on energy generated by chloroplasts it stole from eaten algae. Within about a week, the head regenerates a functioning heart, and in roughly three weeks, it grows an entire replacement body—organs, digestive system, and all.

sources.title: These Solar-Powered Sea Slugs Can Regrow A Decapitated Body

cards.title: No, You Do Not Swallow Eight Spiders a Year in Your Sleep
cards.body: The claim that the average person swallows eight spiders a year in their sleep is a total urban myth. Spiders perceive a sleeping human as a giant, vibrating, warm hill with noisy rhythmic breathing and a booming heartbeat—hardly an inviting destination. Furthermore, human breathing and swallowing reflexes would make inhaling a bug without coughing or waking up virtually impossible. Spiders want nothing to do with your mouth.

sources.title: Fact or Fiction?: People Swallow Spiders While They Sleep
Spider Myths: You Swallow Spiders in Your Sleep

cards.title: An Average Fluffy Cloud Weighs Over a Million Pounds
cards.body: Cumulus clouds look like weightless puffs of cotton floating across the summer sky, but an average one weighs roughly 1.1 million pounds—about 500,000 kilograms. That is roughly the weight of 100 adult African elephants. A cloud can float despite this immense mass because its billions of tiny water droplets are spread out across a cubic kilometer of sky, supported from underneath by warmer, denser rising air.

sources.title: How Much Does a Cloud Weigh?

cards.title: Birds Cannot Feel the Heat of Even the Spiciest Chili Peppers
cards.body: Chili peppers pack heat thanks to capsaicin, an irritant designed to punish mammalian teeth and stomachs. But birds feel zero heat from even the hottest peppers. Birds lack the specific pain receptor on nerve endings that binds with capsaicin in mammals. Because birds pass chili seeds through their digestive tracts completely unharmed, chili plants effectively bribe birds to scatter their seeds across wide territories without losing them to grinding mammalian molars.

sources.title: Are Birds Immune to Hot Pepper Spice?

cards.title: Some Giant Tarantulas Keep Tiny 'Pet' Frogs for Pest Control
cards.body: In the Peruvian Amazon, burrowing tarantulas frequently share their homes with tiny dotted humming frogs in a strange cross-species alliance. The massive, venomous spider could easily crush the frog, but leaves it unharmed. In return, the tiny amphibian acts as a live-in pest control officer, eating ants and tiny parasites that would otherwise swarm and destroy the spider's delicate egg sacs. The frog gets free 24-hour security.

sources.title: Pet frogs and giant spiders in the Amazon

quizzes.question: How does the severed head of the sea slug Elysia marginata stay alive while regrowing its body?
options: By photosynthesizing using chloroplasts harvested from algae
By slowly digesting its own discarded body tissues
By absorbing dissolved nutrients through its antennae
By entering a dormant state with zero metabolic activity
quizzes.explanation: Elysia marginata survives through kleptoplasty, keeping stolen algal chloroplasts functional inside its head to produce energy until a new body grows.

quizzes.question: Why is the idea that people swallow spiders while asleep considered biologically absurd?
options: Spiders only hunt outdoors and cannot navigate indoor spaces
Breathing vibrations deter spiders, and human reflexes prevent swallowing unnoticed
Human saliva contains enzymes that instantly dissolve spider silk and legs
Spiders are entirely nocturnal and retreat into hiding before humans sleep
quizzes.explanation: Spiders perceive sleeping humans as giant, noisy, vibrating threats, and any creature on the mouth would trigger coughing or swallowing reflexes that wake the person.

quizzes.question: How can a cumulus cloud weighing over a million pounds remain suspended in the air?
options: Its water is turned to steam by direct exposure to solar radiation
It contains high concentrations of trapped helium and hydrogen
Its mass is spread across a massive volume and buoyed by denser rising updrafts
It is held up by magnetic repulsion from the planet's surface
quizzes.explanation: A cloud's huge mass is dispersed into billions of microscopic droplets over roughly a cubic kilometer, easily supported by warmer rising air currents beneath it.

quizzes.question: Why are birds completely unaffected by the extreme spiciness of chili peppers?
options: Their beaks prevent capsaicin oils from contacting any living tissue
They lack the specific pain receptor that capsaicin binds to in mammals
Their stomach acid breaks down capsaicin before it reaches nerves
They produce an enzyme in their mouth that neutralizes pepper heat
quizzes.explanation: Capsaicin activates the TRPV1 receptor in mammals, but avian versions of this receptor do not bind capsaicin, leaving birds immune to the burn.

quizzes.question: What primary service does the dotted humming frog provide to the tarantula sharing its burrow?
options: It croaks loudly to scare away approaching predatory wasps
It eats ants and tiny parasites that prey on the spider's eggs
It secretes moisture to prevent the burrow from drying out
It shares toxic secretions that make the spider poisonous to mammals
quizzes.explanation: The small frog feasts on ants and other tiny invertebrates that would otherwise raid the tarantula's egg sac, receiving safe shelter in return.

guesses.prompt: Roughly how many pounds does an average, single fluffy cumulus cloud weigh?
guesses.explanation: With a volume of about one cubic kilometer and water density of 0.5 grams per cubic meter, an average cumulus cloud holds 1.1 million pounds of water.

misconceptions.claim: The average person swallows eight spiders a year while sleeping.
misconceptions.explanation: This popular statistic is a fabricated urban myth. Spiders actively avoid sleeping humans, and a person's natural reflexes would wake them if one crawled in.

misconceptions.claim: Birds feel the fiery burning sensation of hot chili peppers just like humans do.
misconceptions.explanation: Birds lack the specific pain receptor that capsaicin binds to, allowing them to eat the hottest peppers without feeling any burn.
